title: Which Interest the Relief Share Acts On in a Dispute Rebill
content:
Which interest the relief share acts on, when a rebill is sized on a card under Personal Credit Cards, is read from the cardholder's holdings under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

| What the savings records show | The interest the relief acts on |
|---|---|
| An active savings account whose balance is at least 25000.00 USD, and at least 1 savings deposit posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months | the interest billed to the card account in the last six months added together |
| An active savings account whose balance is below 25000.00 USD, and at least 1 savings deposit posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months | the largest single interest charge ever billed to the card account |
| Neither of those | the interest billed to the card account in the last two months added together |

**Both parts of each row.** An active savings account of the stated balance and at least 1 savings deposit in the last three months are required together. A cardholder with an active savings balance of 30000.00 USD and no savings deposit in that window falls in the third row.

**What the difference is worth.** On a card account whose interest charges were 22.40 USD and 19.10 USD in the last two months and 14.00 USD, 16.20 USD, 22.40 USD and 19.10 USD across the last six months, the first row gives 71.70 USD, the second gives 22.40 USD, being the largest single charge in the card account's whole history of interest, and the third gives 41.50 USD. A balance of exactly 25000.00 USD belongs to the first row, the test being at least that amount.
